Subject: Re: Packaging options for Q3 forecast

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran numbers internally and expect our usage to hover around 250k tokens/month for the first two quarters, with frequent spikes (short-lived) up to ~380k when batch jobs run. Procurement is concerned about two things:

- We don't want an immediate tier upgrade every time we spike; marketing batch jobs are seasonal and bursty.
- We also want the ability to add only the moderation/PII redaction feature to a subset of requests without paying full seat increases.

Can you outline any mechanisms you support for short-term burst credits, a grace threshold before auto-upgrade, and a la carte feature grafting (e.g., enable moderation on specific routes)? If there's a recommended plan composition that minimizes our bill surprise while preserving performance SLAs, please share.

Also, procurement asked whether an annual commit with a modest discount makes sense given our projected growth—what's typical there?

Thanks,
Samira

Hi Samira — great questions, thanks for laying out the usage profile. High-level options that fit your requirements: 

1) Burst credit bucket + soft-thresholding (recommended)
   - You buy a monthly burst bucket (e.g., 200k tokens) that applies only to overage bursts; bursts consume from this bucket before any tier change.
   - Soft-threshold: auto-upgrade triggers only after 2 consecutive days above 130% of baseline or 3 spikes in a 30-day window.

2) Commit + buffer credits (best unit economics)
   - Annual commit for baseline (e.g., 250k tokens/mo) with 10–20% discount depending on term and payment schedule. Buffer credits purchased upfront cover spikes; unused buffer credits roll into a credit pool applied at renewal.

3) Feature grafting (route-level entitlements)
   - We support per-route feature entitlements: you can enable moderation/PII redaction on specific API routes or user cohorts. Pricing for grafted features is metered by usage of that feature (per-call add-on), not by full seat. This avoids paying for feature seats across all traffic.

Attached is a tailored proposal with three scenarios and estimated monthly spend at your spike profile. I also included an example auto-upgrade policy and the exact wording we put in contracts to avoid surprise upgrades.

If you want, I can run a short simulation with your spreadsheet and show which scenario keeps month-to-month variance under a defined threshold.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Soft-threshold auto-upgrade policy (2 days >130% or 3 spikes in 30d)
- A route-level moderation add-on priced as $0.0025/call (they expect ~80k moderation calls in spike months)

Need sign-off on: discount level (12% vs 15%), whether product ok with the proposed soft-threshold language, and whether route-level pricing at $0.0025/call is acceptable or should be higher.

Thoughts?

Alex — I ran the numbers with finance and product. Quick notes: 

- Discount: 12% is the ceiling for a straight annual commit with our current Q3 quota pressure. 15% requires Sales Ops approval and a documented case (Strategic logo, >$X ARR, or multi-region commitment). MediPact looks mid-market (likely $90–140k ARR), so 12% is reasonable.
- Soft-threshold language: Product agrees to the policy but wants a clause: soft-threshold can be overridden by sustained 30-day averages; if monthly average exceeds baseline for 30 consecutive days we convert to the higher tier for next billing cycle. That protects capacity planning.
- Route add-on pricing: $0.0025/call is low if moderation includes PII redaction + OCR. Recommend $0.0035/call for combined moderation/redaction. If they only want lightweight keyword moderation, $0.0025 is fine.

If you think they're a strategic reference customer, escalate to Sales Ops for 15% or offer the $3k onboarding credit + 12% discount. Otherwise push 12% + $3k onboarding credit.

—Priyom
Director, Commercial Strategy
